items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: his influence from Horace Silver and all of this

ctx.x: I had the pleasure of chatting with him earlier this week and he was talking about Cecil Taylor and I was sort of happy to hear that he described Cecil as a man who was happy most of the time. And the reason I say that is because I think a lot of people feel that music that is described as free jazz is often angry or reactive. And I wonder how you feel about that?

Yeah, I think that’s a real oversimplification. I think that there definitely were political and sociological underpinnings to a lot of that movement and so possibly they’re hearing some of that. But I know I read a review once of something of mine and they said why is Marilyn Crispell so angry and I was like what? I’m not angry. You know it’s just about a particular energy and tonality and when I started playing more romantic music and more ballads, whatever, someone I had played with for a long time in the sort…
Did you go to the piano and try to figure out how and — how is he able to sound like that?
